source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili.
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, needing nothing from God, and not recognizing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of his: one indeed, made in a human being in a plague, knowing to bear weakness, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led like a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of his hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and remembering his own dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might rescue them; but the second, in which he will come over the clouds, bringing a day which is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and killing the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering wheat into a barn, but burning chaff with unquenchable fire.

pass_b_english: The spiritual disciple truly receives the Spirit of God, who from the beginning was present to men in all of God's dispositions, announced future things, showed present things, and narrated past things; this disciple judges all, yet is judged by no one.
He judges the nations, creatures who serve the Creator rather than the Creator, and who consume their whole operation in vain with a reprobate mind.

He also judges the Jews, because they do not perceive the word of liberty, nor are they willing to go free when they have a present liberator; instead, they pretend to serve outside the law at an unseasonable time, as if God needed anything, and they do not recognize the advent of Christ, which he accomplished for the salvation of men, nor are they willing to understand, since all the prophets announced his two advents: one, in which he was made in a human being in a plague, knowing how to bear weakness, sitting on a foal of a donkey, a stone rejected by the builders, led like a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of his hands; gathering, however, the scattered sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, remembering his own dead who had slept, and descending to them so that he might rescue them; the other, in which he will come on the clouds, bringing a day that is like a burning furnace, striking the earth with the word of his mouth, killing the impious with the spirit through his lips, holding a winnowing fan in his hand, purging his threshing floor, gathering wheat into his barn, but burning chaff with unquenchable fire.
